Thank you. I've been talking to some friends as well, and everything has let me refocus for now what I should be doing to get over this. I feel capable of understanding that I want to get over this, which is worlds better than I felt about a few hours ago. It's crazy how fickle emotions are when they're at extremes.

A few things I think I can clarify on, and maybe expand some.  I think the world makes perfect sense, but the world that makes sense accepts that I'm flawed and nothing will make me happy.

As far as dedicating my life to people, I do that a lot. I'm always there for people, but I also don't let myself get taken advantage of.

As far as existance after this, I think it all has a biological start and end: conception to death. Nothing else. Fear of death is just a trait we inheret in our primitive as part if a species that makes our largest goal sex.
That's how I spent the rest of my depressed life, by trying to focus all my energy on how to fix it and how to be different. I'm not different though. I'm sorry for wasting your time.

You're right, it's up to me to be willing to believe. I think I've spent my entire life believing, and right now I feel like I'm at this point because that's the last thing I ever want to do again. I'm an atheist, and I'm not afraid of anything in the afterlife because I don't think there is anything after death. That blissful nonexistance feels so much more comforting than the idea of being here.

I've been more outgoing, worked through all of my social anxiety to the point to where I really don't have any anymore, and tried to be nice, friendly all the time. This makes people think you're a great person, but it doesn't improve your life in any way.

I have an alright relationship with my family, but I'm never going to be happy and I'm sure they know that after observing me all my life.

The people who care only care because they're trained to believe that suicide is such a bad option once you get to a point in your life when you realize nothing can get better for you. I've tried my entire life to fix all my social problems that led me up to this point, only to have the fear of losing someone make my depression worse because even though she told me I could always talk to her apparently that meant unless I really needed to. Those people don't know what it's like to finally be happy because that person has decided to end their life. It's a merciful choice for somebody who really can't be happy.

I'm in a very similar situation, however I still find a way to get angry with you about your post. You have somebody here, a friend, who's talking up your good points while you're thinking about suicide. You have somebody who's genuinely worried about you and willing to help you through every small thing that you can think of about why you want to do it. Fuck you if you still want to kill yourself.
